decision: Within the same original member first-breakout opportunities, after the original leader's first adjacent close decline has already occurred, does retaining the member's own pre-decline closing-price level improve empirical account and trade outcomes?
objective: Empirical repeatable small-loss/larger-win research. Human corrections override stale annual30/per-trade30 and3-10-day goal wording. No profit, payoff, win-rate, average-winner or holding-duration acceptance hurdles. Preserve every fixed comparison and sparse/null outcome.
novelty: A first adjacent price decline followed by a member's own fixed-level retention before its existing first breakout. Earlier local succession used persistentQ, two-day numerical rank overtake and anchorQ failure. This does not require Q failure, relative rank overtake, traded-value crossover, pseudo-anchor or market-date admission.

validity.calendar: Exact ordered unique source-calendar slots including warmup, numeric reads at or before registered end. No compressed gaps.

validity.required: For the anchor, exact adjacent prices from A until the first known down-close or first required unknown or T. After a first down-close is proven, later anchor bars are not required. Member retention requires every exact valid slot P-1..T-1; its T breakout is inherited and checked against raw evidence.

clock.AandT: A and T retain their parent meaning. T is the parent's first close strictly above its preceding five exact highs within A+1..A+5. Never search a later member breakout to obtain a desired sequence.
clock.firstDown: For EACH original opportunity separately, scan source slots d=A+1..T in order. At each d require valid raw anchor bars at d-1,d. First strict close_d<close_d-1 establishes P; equality is not a decline. Stop at this P. If a required pair is unknown before P, stop with firstDownUnknown; do not skip unknowns to pick a later decline. If all pairs through T are known and none declines, noDownThroughT.
clock.prefix: The result uses only the opportunity's A..T prefix. Never compute a final A+5 state and backfill an earlier T. A known P remains fixed if the anchor later becomes unknown; those later bars are irrelevant to this event definition.
clock.ordering: P<T gives a prior down-close event. P=T is sameDayDown and does not qualify. T=A+1 cannot have a strictly prior down-close. NoDownThroughT and sameDayDown are known non-admissions, not censored. Parent members without an original T remain in inherited lifecycle dispositions; no new opportunity is synthesized.
clock.terminology: First adjacent close decline is not necessarily a material peak drawdown, sustained leader weakness or lost leadership. A first decline of any strictly negative size counts; no fitted amplitude threshold.

retention.reference: For proven P<T use member close at exact P-1 as fixed reference R. Observe member closes on every exact slot P..T-1, excluding T. At least one observation follows from P<T; no extra duration gate.
retention.known: Both policies require complete valid member raw bars P-1..T-1. Preserve every readable close and independent unknown/breach evidence even when common support is unknown.
retention.predicate: retained iff every member close on P..T-1>=R; equality passes. A single strict breach fails permanently for this opportunity, even if the member recovers or breaks out on T. No tolerance, rounding, alternate reference, moving-average or threshold search.
retention.diagnostics: Keep first breach date, all known breach dates, observation length and elapsed A-to-P/P-to-T slots. These explain coverage only and never define new gates. If reference is unknown, breach comparisons remain unknown; do not impute.
